correctness.rationale: A zero-free point belongs exactly to the Sturmian minimal aperiodic subshift, so periodic points always have recognizable zero markers. Cyclic marker cuts are uniquely decomposed into finite Sturmian factors; counting length-m labeled periodic points with k distinguished markers gives P_m=m/k [z^m]F(z)^k. Summing yields zeta=1/(1-F). Rational F has an eventually recurring integer coefficient sequence and the Skolem–Mahler–Lech zero-set theorem gives eventual periodic S; the converse follows by arithmetic-geometric summation. For nonperiodic S, nonrational integer F of exact radius one invokes Pólya–Carlson, and a meromorphic continuation of zeta across any unit-circle arc would analytically continue F on a subarc. Marker-free Sturmian part precludes soficity. The statement correctly distinguishes unit-circle natural boundary from Taylor radius.
